name: ARA
summary: An array of deep radio stations near the South Pole searches for ultra-high-energy neutrinos interacting in Antarctic ice.
physics_targets: Cosmogenic and astrophysical neutrinos above tens of PeV
detection_principle: Antennas buried in boreholes detect coherent Askaryan emission from particle cascades. Timing across a station reconstructs a radio source and rejects surface and instrumental backgrounds; a phased-array trigger has also been deployed.

sites.name: Antarctica; ice near the South Pole
sites.location: Antarctica; ice near the South Pole

status.label: Multiple stages
status.evidence: The physical station array is implemented and recent papers analyse its recorded exposures; uninterrupted 2026 operation is not inferred from the old homepage.

timeline.event: Deep stations and a phased-array system deployed.
Progress toward the first array-wide diffuse-neutrino search reported; the fully analysed sample was still in development.

collaboration.name: ARA Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Array
key_parameters.value: Five autonomous stations with approximately 2 km spacing

key_parameters.name: Main search scale
key_parameters.value: Ultra-high energies, typically above 10–100 PeV depending on station and analysis

results.summary: The cited contribution describes an ongoing array-wide search using approximately 28 station-years. Its projected sensitivity and progress toward a fully analysed sample are not a completed unblinded flux measurement or a neutrino discovery.

science_scope: Parameters refer to the named apparatus or explicitly identified design phase. Projections describe sensitivity goals and are not observations.
